ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a six-membered ring structure containing two NH and one urea carbonyl; above the ring is connected an ethyl ester group C(=O)OCH2CH3, and on the right side is connected an Ar aryl group. The upper-left ring carbon bears a protonated hydroxyl/water leaving group, labeled H2O+, and this carbon is also connected to a methyl group; the adjacent upper ring carbon is labeled H and is connected to the ethyl ester substituent. The curved arrow in the figure indicates that the electrons of the adjacent C-H bond move toward between the two adjacent ring carbons, while water departs as the leaving group. Reasoning: According to the arrow pushing, this is a dehydration elimination step; H is removed from the ester-substituted ring carbon bearing H, the C-H bond electrons form a C=C double bond between this carbon and the left-side methyl-substituted ring carbon, while H2O+ on the left-side carbon leaves. The remaining parts stay unchanged: the two NH in the ring, the urea carbonyl C=O, the ethyl ester C(=O)OCC, and the aryl substituent are all retained. Therefore the product’s corresponding SMILES is CC(N1)=C(C(OCC)=O)C(c2ccccc2)NC1=O.
